compliance.seismic: Designed to comply with Zone 4 earthquake requirements per NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 3

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 1828.8 m (6000 ft)
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing; short term 5 to 93 percent
environmental.operating-temp: 0 C to 40 C (32 F to 104 F)
environmental.storage-temp: -40 C to 70 C (-40 F to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.timing: 1PPS and 10 MHz SMB connectors and a PTP Ethernet SFP port

performance.packet-buffer: deep buffer from hybrid memory cubes (HMC)
performance.throughput: 5.76 Tbps and 2 Bpps of forwarding capacity (Q5 ASICs); 288 x 10 GbE, 72 x 40 GbE or 24 x 100 GbE ports (Table 2)

physical.mounting: four-post rack kit in the box; spare kits EX4500-4PST-RMK
physical.weight: 31.1 kg (68.6 lb) with four AC supplies and three fan modules fitted; 30.8 kg (67.8 lb) for the DC build (Table 30)

platform.asic: Q5 packet forwarding ASICs with hybrid memory cubes
platform.storage: two 25 GB SSDs (the hardware inventory text also names a 25 GB NAND flash drive)

power.psu-ac-input: 100 to 127 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC at 50 to 60 Hz, 12.9 A at 100-120 VAC (Table 21); each supply has one input
power.psu-dc-input: -48 to -60 VDC rated, -40 to -72 VDC operating range, 40 A maximum; a 40 A breaker is recommended
power.psu-redundancy: four bays, 2N recommended; one supply at 220 VAC or two at 110 VAC run the 72Q

thermal.airflow: port-to-FRU (airflow out, front-to-back); three 80 W fan modules at 150 CFM each, and fans in the supplies
thermal.heat-dissipation: 3,583 BTU/hr typical and 4,862 BTU/hr maximum (Tables 21 and 25)

configs.description: The QFX10002-72Q as shipped (Table 1 and Table 30): four 1600 W AC supplies and three fan modules, all with port-to-FRU airflow.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: The DC build QFX10002-72Q-DC (Table 1): four 1600 W DC supplies. Mixing AC and DC supplies in one chassis is not supported.
configs.name: dc

configs.description: The spare chassis QFX10002-72Q-CHAS-S (Table 3). The guide lists the chassis, the fan module and the supplies as separate spares and does not say what a spare chassis ships with, so it is read as the chassis alone with every bay open (estimated). It takes either feed once supplies are fitted.
configs.name: s

gaps.note: The HPE PSNow datasheet a00150807enw was tried once and the transfer failed (HTTP/2 stream error), so no datasheet is cited and no figure comes from one.
gaps.wanted: the HPE PSNow QFX10002 datasheet, for the bundle part numbers

gaps.note: The 72Q studio photographs (qfx10002-72q-front-high and -rear-high, tried once each) returned an HTML 404 page, so the 72Q has no studio photograph. What it prints, its colour and its cage orientation are read from the guide's figures and from the 36Q photographs, which share the panel art.

The guide's four-post procedure names no ear distance in millimetres and draws the rails only in perspective (Figures 33 to 35), so no ears position is written, and the spare kit EX4500-4PST-RMK is left out of chassis.kits in this slice.
gaps.wanted: the rail drawing and ear distances, and the four-post kit as a kit contract

airflow.note: Description and Table 17 - every QFX10002 has port-to-FRU airflow (airflow out, AFO, front-to-back): air enters through the vents of the port panel and leaves through the FRU panel. The guide lists no back-to-front fan module or supply, so the device has no airflow configuration. The module handles are gold in the guide's tables and orange in the photograph (the photograph wins; see the module contracts).

colour.note: Median of the bare front face in the 36Q photograph (#c4c5c7 at the left margin, #bebfc1 and #cfcfcf near the right). The rear chassis reads #75777a in the rear photograph. The fan faces and the supply handles read #ec640e and #f94e16 in the photograph.

drawing-vs-photo.note: sources-disagree, checked on the 36Q photograph because the 72Q has none, and the real device wins for everything printed. Figures 12 and 21 print PWR, MAJ, STS and MIN with the word ALARM in a bracket, the SFP legends MGMT and ETH, and 10MHz; the 36Q photograph prints PWR, MJR, STA and MNR, the legends MGMT and PTP, and 10M, with no bracket and no ALARM. The guide's own text (Table 16) names the lamps PWR, STA, MJR and MIN. The silkscreen follows the photograph, on the reading that the 72Q's management panel is the 36Q's. Figure 12 draws a laser-radiation label as a white box with printed words at the left end of the upper band; the 36Q photograph shows its label yellow, so the plate is drawn yellow and its words, which cannot be read at this resolution, are not drawn.

envelope.note: Table 30, Physical Specifications for the QFX10002: 3.46 in. (8.8 cm) high, 17.36 in. (44.1 cm) wide, 31 in. (78.7 cm) deep "without handles for fans or power supplies". The height is carried as 88.0 mm, the 8.8 cm of the table (3.46 in. is 87.9 mm), 2RU. The face is the body between the folds with no ears drawn. The installation text gives 19 in. (48.26 cm) over the front mounting brackets. The depth 787.0 mm is the 78.7 cm of the table. The table gives the 72Q 68.6 lb (31.1 kg) with four AC supplies and three fans, and 67.8 lb (30.8 kg) with DC supplies. The install topic gives the same figures, so no weight disagrees.

hundred-gig-marks.note: Table 11 and the 100-Gbps text - "ports marked with a fine black line underneath the socket" take QSFP28 and run at 100 GbE, which disables the two neighbours (Table 12). The line is drawn under the lower cage of the first and third column of each group, in both bands, 24 ports in all as the table says (1, 5, 7, 11 and so on to 35, then 37, 41, 43, 47 and so on to 71). Figure 12 draws a "100G" legend at the left end of each band. The 36Q photograph prints neither the legend nor a visible line, so the legend is not drawn and the lines are drawn thin, as the text says and the drawing shows.

logo.note: The maker's logo at the top right is not drawn. It is reserved as the region logo-zone, 26.0 x 8.0 mm, read off the 36Q photograph (the logo spans 409.5 to 434.2 across and 1.3 to 7.4 down) and shifted 0.9 mm with the panel. The model name below it is plain text and is drawn.

mgmt-panel.note: Figure 21 (g050373) callouts 1 to 9 and Figure 12, the same panel as the 36Q's, measured on Figure 12 per axis. Callout 1 is the em0 RJ-45 (1000BASE-T) management port centred at 393.3, 54.1; callout 2 the RJ-45 console (CON) at 413.0, 53.9; callout 3 the reset button, a round recess at 412.9, 63.2 below the console; callout 4 the four status lamps at 425.8 and 430.9 across and 51.9 and 56.9 down; callout 5 the em1 SFP management port (MGMT) at 381.3 across and 68.0 down; callout 6 the PTP Ethernet SFP port (the drawing labels it ETH, the 36Q photograph PTP) right of it at 396.3; callout 7 the PPS SMB at 415.1, 72.5; callout 8 the 10 MHz SMB at 423.1, 72.5; callout 9 the USB port, upright, at 431.8, 70.9 with the USB symbol below it. Two small round lamps above the two SFP cages at 393.1 and 398.9 across and 65.1 down are the SFP port lamps (Table 15 - one link and activity lamp). The two cages are 14.25 mm wide on a 15.0 mm pitch. Jack sizes come from the registry; the drawing's housing outlines are not used for size.

mounting.note: Mounting a QFX10002 in a Rack and Table 45 - a four-post kit ships in the box (two front mounting rails, two rear mounting blades, 24 flathead screws) and spare kits are ordered as EX4500-4PST-RMK. The rails fit the sides of the chassis (Figure 34) and the front rails may be flush with either end of the switch. The rack must have its rails 28 to 31 in. (71.1 to 78.7 cm) apart front to back. The guide gives no ear distance in millimetres and no rail drawing that can be measured and says the chassis must be supported at all four corners, so no ear position and no kit is written. EX4500-4PST-RMK is not listed under chassis.kits here (it is a shared four-post kit and follows in a later slice). See the gap rack-mounting.

port-leds.note: Figure 17 and Table 13 - each QSFP+ port has one bicolour LED, "triangle shaped". The strip between the two cages of a column draws an up triangle at its left, four small slots and a down triangle at its right. The up triangle is the upper port's lamp and the down triangle the lower port's, as the triangles point at their ports and as the library's SFP+ stacks draw them. The lamp centres are 7.0 mm left and 7.4 mm right of the column centre in the drawing, which the drawing keeps unequal. The slots are drawn as one dark plate per column. Table 13 gives the states: green steady is a link (all four sub-channels up when channelized), green blinking is activity, slow green is the beacon, amber steady is some but not all sub-channels up (Junos 15.1X53-D21 and CPLD 1.16 and later) and amber blinking is activity on some sub-channels.

port-numbering.note: Figure 12 prints 0, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 34 above the upper row of the upper band and 1, 7, 13, 19, 25, 31 and 35 below it, and 36, 42, 48, 54, 60, 66 and 70 above the lower band's upper row and 37, 43, 49, 55, 61, 67 and 71 below it. Each column holds the even port above the odd one and the ports run left to right, and the upper band holds 0 to 35 and the lower band 36 to 71. THE 36Q PHOTOGRAPH PRINTS FEWER NUMBERS THAN ITS DRAWING (only 1, 34 and 35 - see the 36Q's port-numbering), so the 72Q may print fewer than Figure 12 draws. With no photograph of the 72Q, Figure 12 (guide page 25), the maker's drawing, is the evidence and is followed, so the confidence is drawing, with that risk noted. Numbering starts at 0, as the guide's CLI examples count (port 0 to port 71). Interface names are not printed on the metal and the guide does not state them, so none is carried.

ports.note: Figure 12 and Table 11, counted - 72 QSFP+ cages in four rows of 18 columns: two bands, each two rows of 18 columns in six groups of three, each group one six-port (6XQSFP+) cage, with a 5.65 mm gutter between groups (the 62.65 mm group step less three 19.0 mm columns) carrying a column of hexagonal vent holes. Cells sit on the registry's 19.0 mm ganged QSFP pitch. The first column's left edge is at 8.19 mm. The upper band's rows are at 11.4 and 27.4 mm and the lower band's at 52.3 and 68.3 mm (row step 16.0 mm, which leaves 6.4 mm between a cage's bottom edge and the next cage's top for the lamp strip). The lower band is the 36Q's row positions exactly. Figure 12 sits 3 px (0.9 mm) further right inside its frame than the 36Q's Figure 19 does, for the cage block and the management panel alike, and each device is measured on its own figure. Counts confirmed by Table 11.

power-supplies.note: Tables 4 and 5, Table 30 and the redundancy text - the 72Q has four bays numbered horizontally from the top left to the bottom right, ships with four 1600 W supplies, and the guide's example output lists the supplies as Power Supply 2 and 3 on a 72Q running two. At 220 VAC one supply runs the switch and at 110 VAC two are needed. The guide recommends twice what is needed (2N), with feed A on supplies 0 or 1 and feed B on 2 or 3, and the remaining slots covered with QFX10002-PWR-BLNK. Mixing AC and DC supplies is not supported.

rear.note: Figure 4 (g050372, the 72Q) and Figure 5 (g050404, the 36Q), measured per axis from the rear left edge (the chassis right side as seen from the front). Power supply bays are 74.1 x 40.6 mm at x 8.8 and 90.4 across and y 1.7 and 43.5 down. Fan module faces are 81.0 x 81.7 mm at x 172.0, 260.9 and 349.8 and y 3.7, on an 88.9 mm pitch. The ESD socket is centred at 436.6, 24.1 with the ESD symbol below it. Fan numbers 0, 1 and 2 with a fan icon and a lamp are printed at 3.8 mm left of each face, the lamp at y 77.9. Power symbols with the digits 0 and 2 are printed at x 86.9 between the supply columns and 1 and 3 at x 168.2 between the right column and the first fan, at y 9.0 and 49.8 (the digits 4.6 mm lower). Two round fixings sit between the supply columns at y 20.8 and 61.4. A vertical legend at the left edge reads "AC INPUT:100-240V ~ 60-50Hz 14A" and "DC INPUT:-48V TO-60V = 40A (FOR EACH POWER SUPPLY)" in Figure 4.

rear-photo.note: qfx10002-36q-rear-high is labelled as the 36Q and shows four supplies, ACDC 1600W Platinum labels on the fan hubs and a legend ending in 14A, which is what Figure 4 prints for the 72Q. THE 72Q HAS NO STUDIO PHOTOGRAPH: Juniper's image-library addresses qfx10002-72q-front-high and qfx10002-72q-rear-high were tried once each and returned an HTML 404 page. The 36Q photographs (qfx10002-36q-front-high and -rear-high, which share the management panel, the cages and the rear panel) were used to check what is printed and how it is coloured. The HPE PSNow datasheet a00150807enw was tried once and the transfer failed, so no datasheet is cited and no figure comes from one. No mechanical drawing, 3D model or Visio stencil of the QFX10002 was found in the sources that could be read.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md) turns the lower cage of a belly to belly pair by 180 degrees. It is not applied here, because the 36Q photograph shows both cages of a column the same way up (the dark module bar high and the silver latch low in each opening, 15.5 mm apart) and Figures 7, 12 and 19 of the guide draw both rows alike. No photograph of the 72Q exists, so the reading is carried from the 36Q, whose cages and panel art the 72Q shares, and is estimated. The lamp strip lies between the rows.

usb-and-slots.note: The guide names no USB revision (Figure 21 callout 9, "USB port"), and the 36Q photograph shows a black tongue, which is neither colour the library's skins carry, so the white USB 2.0 skin is used and no 3.0 is claimed. The four small slots between the two lamps of each column are drawn as one dark plate 9.3 x 2.8 mm (the drawing shows two rows of four), centred 0.3 mm right of the column centre.

vents.note: Figure 12 - a hexagonal punching above the upper band, between the two bands and below the lower band, a column of seven hexagons in each gutter of each band, and fields beside and below the management panel. They are drawn as repeating patterns inside simplified outlines and not hole for hole, and the stepped outline of the field next to the logo is simplified to two rectangles.
